newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Exchange to list textile firm Berdan.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Exchange to list textile firm Berdan.

text.p: The Istanbul Stock Exchange said the shares of Turkish textile producer Berdan Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. would be listed on the national market on March 27.
It said the opening price would be 12,500 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share.
The company had sold to public 100 billion lira nominal-valued shares last week when raising its capital to 520 billion lira from 420 billion.

Offer manager ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Istanbul securities said 40 percent of the 100 billion lira nominal offer was sold to 40,000 domestic individual investors, 20 percent to 32 domestic institutional investors and 40 percent to 13 foreign investors.
LCF Edmund De Rotchild Banque bought 9.6 percent and Etoile Capital Asset Management bought 9.1 percent of the total offer, ABN said.
Berdan which posted a 441.1 billion lira net profit in 1996, said it would keep distributable profits under the extraordinary reserves account.

As an integrated plant with spinning, weaving, dyeing and finishing units and a product portfolio of polyviscose, including polyester, viscose, wool, linen and their blends, Berdan has an annual output capacity of 13 million metres.
